question: Why did the return rate spike last month?
sql:
SELECT FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m', oi.created_at) AS month,
       p.brand,
       COUNT(*) AS items,
       ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(COUNTIF(oi.status = 'Returned'), COUNT(*)), 3) AS return_rate
FROM order_items AS oi
JOIN products AS p ON p.id = oi.product_id
WHERE oi.created_at >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 90 DAY)
GROUP BY month, p.brand
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
ORDER BY month, return_rate DESC
report: Return rate is returned items divided by all items ordered in the period. First confirm the spike exists by comparing the last three months overall. Then break the rate down by brand, and by category within the brand that moved, to find where it comes from. Ignore groups with fewer than 20 items: their rates jump around by chance.
